svg.title: Star Tracker Controller wiring: Pi to ST-4 through optocouplers
svg.text: Wiring: Raspberry Pi to the mount's ST-4 port
Pin numbers are the Pi's physical header pins; GPIO numbers (BCM) in brackets. Build one opto channel per guide line.
Odd pins on the left, even on the right.
common: all opto pin 3s → ST-4 pin 2 (contact 5)
Gold contacts facing you, clip at
the back, tip up, cable down.
sit together at one end; RA− (pin 6)
Seen from the other side, or tip down,
left and right swap. Don't go by wire
For trackers with a manual DEC axis: 28BYJ-48 motor on a ULN2003 board.
Each PC817 the right way round: the dot marks pin 1.
Mount on, lead plugged in, Pi NOT connected: a meter
reads about 3–5 V between each guide line and common.
Software keeps every output low at start and after pulses.
If a dither moves the stars the wrong way,
swap that axis's two wires (RA+ with RA−).
Pinouts differ between drawings: trust your meter.
